eyebrow: Golu 2026 · An update from our home
title: 2026 Golu - The OLD and the NEW
author: Archana
paragraphs: Mahalaya Amavaasai descended on us graciously this year over the Fall Break weekend. This meant all of us could crowd around Raj and deliciously trouble him as he religiously put up the steps. I couldn’t believe my eyes watching the Teen and the Tween unwrapping these now vintage dolls, naming them and correcting Raj’s order in which they should be displayed. It feels like only a few years ago that Arjun was 1 year old and grabbing an apple from the fruit basket we kept in front of the Golu. The years fly by so soon! My wish is to hold tightly on to every memory and savor them each year. With luck, I can taunt the kids when they are all grown up by cooing some stories into their kids’ ears. There’s your case for traditions and rituals. They give you permission to pause, repeat and enjoy each year, each stage of life.

This nostalgia pushed me to get the ancient dolls out - the ones from Raj’s first years of Golu and combine with some of Simply Pottery treasures that Arjun and Janvi paint and bake to make the last padi of the Golu. Birds and Animals from all stages of life including a Lego Peacock, Harry Potter’s Patronus - The Stag, Pigeons, Owls, Flamingos, Elephants, Unicorns and our favorite Bluey and Bingo. We put in tradespeople like vegetable-seller, wood-cutter and saree-weaver who are an important part of the economy. We gave the Auto and Lorry which still serves as the life blood of Chennai moving people and goods an important place.

We also formed an assembly line to make the gift bags that we lovingly curate every year and brainstormed ways to improve speed while optimizing for workers working on their favorite station, bonding between workers and encouraging conversations on what gifts we added last year. If that’s not a systems engineering problem, I don’t know what is 😀

Since we have a Lego-nerd at home who is also a budding Potter-head, he convinced us to add a side Golu to include his favorite Potterverse Lego pieces that he has been working on for many years. Arjun says he was inspired by a dear friend’s Golu where she described each scene of the Ramayana in a blurb as he added little name tents for each scene. These miniatures have a lot of effort and love that goes into them. So be sure to ask questions - Arjun revels in explaining. Wonder where he gets that from? Special mention to Aunt Petunia’s Violet Pudding that sits in 4 Privet Drive about to be smashed on Mrs. Mason.

Artist Janvi made the posters to advertise the theme of each part (Potterverse and Ladies Go Places). She added kolams and signs to the door to welcome our guests. Janvi didn’t want the ladies of India to miss out on the Golu fun. So, we devised a theme to give them their own, rightful place at the table (wink wink). Arjun’s skyline sets and the White House also looked lonely. An elegant solution was born where the ladies go places. Dare to dream and fly, my little dollies!

aside.title: In the collector’s words
aside.author: Arjun
paragraphs: The time for Navratri and Golu is one of the most reminisceable. We get to unwrap the dolls and idols, prepare and package goodybags, and welcome friends to our home. We get to be creative in our displays, and our new Golu’s beloved additions stand thus. Since 2019, I’ve been fond of Legos. I’ve collected a lot over the years and built a vast collection of Legos from all themes. The majority contents from my collection are sets from Harry Potter. Simultaneously, I also collected bird figurines and sculptures. I was a frequent visitor to Simply Pottery, where some of my sculptures originate. My collection has grown with time.

When the Navratri time came, an idea for variety was born. We wanted to reserve one padi for birds and animals from my collection. Some of the most noticeable are the peacock that stands in the middle and Harry Potter’s Patronus (Blue stag). I made sure to include various bird sculptures in their own section. Amma had a genius idea to recruit some bird statues from her ancient Golu set to go with mine. A blend of the ancient and the modern;).

Subsequent to finishing the last padi, Janvi brought up the topic of where the Ladies of India would go. Amma proposed that they can be put on the desk adjacent to the main Golu. Yet I already had a plan to add some more of my Legos there. So a new theme was born: Ladies Go Places. We set up the Ladies of India in a row, and placed my Lego skyline sets in front of them (in a way which both can be seen perfectly). Lego skyline sets consist of all the landmarks in a certain city (Example: Paris) all on one street.

Continuing the theme of Lego, I had a small, unused nightstand at my disposal. My idea was to display sets from Harry Potter movies 2, 3, and 4. Taking inspiration from a friend, I added small pamphlets next to each set, describing what was happening. I feel they also add to the “curated museum” feel. Some sets have moving parts, so if you’d like, I can show you what moves. Take pictures, please!!! Tours are available in English and Tamil!
